```{python}
def number(x, digits=3):
    return "—" if pd.isna(x) else f"{float(x):.{digits}f}"

def interval(row, value="estimate", low="ci_low", high="ci_high", digits=3, scale=1):
    return f"{float(row[value])*scale:.{digits}f} ({float(row[low])*scale:.{digits}f} to {float(row[high])*scale:.{digits}f})"

def effect_pair(model, reference, metric="auc"):
    found = pairs.loc[pairs["model"].eq(model) & pairs["reference"].eq(reference) & pairs["metric"].eq(metric)]
    assert len(found) == 1, f"Expected one paired comparison: {model}, {reference}, {metric}"
    return found.iloc[0]

def delta_text(model, reference, metric="auc"):
    return interval(effect_pair(model, reference, metric), value="difference", digits=4)

def pair_interpretation(model, reference, metric="auc"):
    row = effect_pair(model, reference, metric)
    lower, upper = float(row.ci_low), float(row.ci_high)
    better = lower > 0 if metric == "auc" else upper < 0
    worse = upper < 0 if metric == "auc" else lower > 0
    if better:
        return "the conditional interval favours the first model"
    if worse:
        return "the conditional interval favours the reference model"
    return "the conditional interval includes no difference"

def show_table(frame, caption, note=""):
    table = frame.to_html(index=False, escape=True, border=0, classes="report-table", na_rep="—")
    display(HTML(f'<div class="table-block"><div class="table-caption">{escape(caption)}</div>'
                 f'<div class="table-scroll" tabindex="0">{table}</div>'
                 f'<p class="table-note">{escape(note)}</p></div>'))

assert (FIGURES / "figure_metadata.json").is_file(), "Figure metadata are missing."
figure_meta = json.loads((FIGURES / "figure_metadata.json").read_text())
assert not figure_meta.get("missing_or_empty_source_tables"), "Figures have incomplete inputs."
figure_lookup = {item["name"]: item for item in figure_meta["figures"]}
figure_names = ["correa_model_performance", "correa_predictor_importance", "correa_validation", "correa_predictor_groups", "correa_sensitivity", "study_flow", "performance_dot", "calibration_roc", "water_association", "incremental_water", "permutation_importance", "predictor_group_contributions", "descriptive_prevalence", "historical_coding_comparison"]
for name in figure_names:
    assert name in figure_lookup and (FIGURES / f"{name}.png").is_file(), f"Missing figure: {name}"

def show_figure(name):
    item = figure_lookup[name]
    encoded = base64.b64encode((FIGURES / f"{name}.png").read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
    caption = escape(item["caption"])
    display(HTML(f'<figure class="analysis-figure"><img src="data:image/png;base64,{encoded}" alt="{caption}">'
                 f'<figcaption>{caption}</figcaption></figure>'))

def simple_metric_table(ids):
    rows = []
    for model in ids:
        row = weighted.loc[model]
        rows.append({
            "Model": labels[model], "Role": roles[model],
            "AUC (95% CI)": interval(row, "auc", "auc_low", "auc_high"),
            "Brier (95% CI)": interval(row, "brier", "brier_low", "brier_high"),
            "Log loss (95% CI)": interval(row, "log_loss", "log_loss_low", "log_loss_high"),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

## Structured summary

Five composite figures, with four to six panels each, preserve the original manuscript’s model-comparison bars and blue predictor-importance bars. The main importance figure now displays all 27 predictors, including water, in six panels with a common axis. Updated descriptive tables retain the original no-caries/caries/total comparison and add survey-weighted uncertainty and explicit missingness.

**Question.** How do the 27 demographic, dental and dietary predictors contribute to classification of existing cavitated caries, and how stable are their contributions across held-out survey clusters and model families?

## Scope, provenance and study population

This report evaluates contributions of all measured predictor constructs to current caries classification, using the original data and an audited R reference in the [ENS-dental-caries repository](https://github.com/AmaruSimonAgueroJimenez/ENS-dental-caries/tree/77c107feb56d3f825cd4ad26354b672f8bfebe38). The original `docs/index.qmd` and saved HTML are preserved; the HTML contains the manuscript's reported AUC values. Those saved results identify the reference analysis but are not newly rerun R estimates.

The original Stata attachment was recovered from Andrea Correa's email of 31 July 2023 and reconciled by survey identifier with the supplementary SPSS release. SPSS supplies survey weights, PSUs and additional water-context fields absent from the original Stata file. This is a **Python reanalysis with verified original data**. The [analysis plan](caries-analysis-plan.md) and [R-to-Python audit](r-to-python-migration.md) explain the intentional methodological changes; identical historical `caret` metrics are not an objective.

```{python}

    ("Predictors matching before beverage-month harmonization", f'{source_predictors["n_matching_without_beverage_month_harmonization"]} / {source_predictors["n"]}'),
    ("Predictors matching after documented harmonization", f'{source_predictors["n_matching_after_declared_harmonization"]} / {source_predictors["n"]}'),
    ("Unexplained predictor discrepancies", str(source_predictors["unexpected_discrepancies"])),
]
show_table(pd.DataFrame(source_rows, columns=["Source check", "Verified result"]),
           "Source verification. Original Stata input and supplementary SPSS release.",
           "Source rows occur in different orders, so checks join by survey identifier. Decoded education and indigenous identification agree. Aggregate checks contain no participant identifiers; both file hashes appear in the reproducibility record.")
legacy_water = tables["legacy_water_coding"]
maximum_water_mapping = legacy_water.loc[legacy_water["reported_glasses_per_day"].idxmax()]
display(Markdown(
    f'The recovered water values and R source show that the later Quarto expression converts labelled water values to **factor indices**, preserving order but changing cardinal spacing. Earlier R scripts leave water as a factor. '
    f'For example, {maximum_water_mapping.reported_glasses_per_day:g} reported glasses/day becomes index '
    f'{int(maximum_water_mapping.original_r_factor_index)}. The Python analysis retains the reported numeric glasses/day. '
    'These are codes for individual observed quantities, not documented low/medium/high intake groups. A separate controlled encoding sensitivity is reported below. '
    'Questionnaire-conditional and original unconditional skip recoding happen to give identical values in this observed dataset; the revised rules explicitly distinguish structural non-consumption from nonresponse.'
))
```

The original R program uses an individual-level training/test partition with internal cross-validation and omits survey fitting weights and PSU grouping. The Python analysis groups survey clusters, uses weights where supported and learns statistical preprocessing within training folds. These are substantive changes to development and evaluation, so historical AUCs should not be compared as if they arose from the same validation experiment.

The newly recovered original materials confirm a requested change from categorical to numeric water on 24 September 2024. The preserved implementation converts factor levels to numerical indices. Water bands were proposed on 22 November, after the October importance spreadsheet; no implementation or output using those bands was found. The dietary supplement presents water as mean (standard deviation), which establishes its descriptive presentation, not the representation supplied to every historical algorithm.

The original Word chart matches all 11 leading scores in the recovered spreadsheet exactly: water is third, at 53.9819 on a rescaled 0–100 scale. The spreadsheet ranks 90 encoded terms representing 27 predictors, including seven single numeric columns and 83 category indicators. Later October/November discussions explicitly intend mean decrease in accuracy, superseding earlier Gini terminology. However, the preserved QMD omits `importance=TRUE`; archived caret 6.0-94 defaults and the recovered single-column `Overall` cache strongly support rescaled Gini under that code. The fitted forest and raw importance matrix remain unavailable, so the exact runtime metric cannot be certified. This separates the documented intention from implementation evidence. [randomForest fitting documentation](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/randomForest/html/randomForest.html).

These historical scores are not directly comparable with the revised held-out, unscaled Brier-score permutation importance of whole original predictors. The [historical analysis audit](historical-analysis-audit.md) documents the source matches, chronology, metric discrepancy and an original legume-category translation error. The subsequent matched-coding refits are reported below as a separate post hoc extension.

ENS is a cross-sectional, stratified, multistage survey. Published documentation describes an oral examination by trained nurses during the second home visit. Eligibility in other oral-health publications differs from the present dentate domain and should not be imposed on this analysis. [Margozzini et al., 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7479467/)

```{python}
    f'Weighted caries prevalence was **{interval(overall, digits=1, scale=100)}%**, compared with **{overall.unweighted_prevalence:.1%}** unweighted. '

))
show_figure("descriptive_prevalence")
```

The outcome is at least one currently decayed permanent tooth, obtained from valid upper- and lower-jaw counts and verified against the original Stata outcome. Completely edentulous people are outside this target population. This measure is neither DMFT nor incident disease; participants without current decay can have substantial prior dental disease or tooth loss. Remaining teeth is a concurrent dental measure, potentially affecting both opportunity to observe decay and model performance.

## Exposures, predictors and data quality

The full comparison uses eight demographic/dental predictors and 19 dietary constructs. Water is self-reported glasses/day. Available metadata do not establish glass volume, fluoride concentration, individual fluoride exposure or substitution for sugary drinks. The three-variable extension adds household supply, recent rural/well/spring water use and dental attendance. These are available contextual variables, but household supply need not be the source of each glass, and attendance may follow disease.

```{python}
#| label: predictor-definitions
#| echo: false
dictionary = tables["variable_dictionary"].set_index("variable")
base_features = model_manifest["models"]["spline_base"]["features"]
full_features = model_manifest["models"]["logistic"]["features"]
diet_features = [name for name in full_features if name not in base_features]
extra_features = [name for name in model_manifest["models"]["spline_extended"]["features"] if name not in full_features]
assert len(base_features) == 8 and len(diet_features) == 19 and len(extra_features) == 3
display(Markdown('**Demographic/dental block:** ' + '; '.join(dictionary.loc[name, "description"] for name in base_features) + '.'))
diet_display = dictionary.loc[diet_features, ["description", "units"]].reset_index(drop=True)
diet_display.columns = ["Dietary construct", "Unit / coding"]
show_table(diet_display, "Table 2. The 19 dietary predictors in the full models.",
           "Fruit and vegetable portions refer to a consumption day, with zero assigned to structural nonconsumers. They are not daily averages. Beverage frequencies are occasions per day, not glasses per day.")
missing = tables["predictor_missingness"].query("missing > 0").copy()
missing["Predictor"] = missing["variable"].map(dictionary["description"])
missing["Missing (%)"] = missing["percent_missing"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.2f}")
show_table(missing[["Predictor", "missing", "Missing (%)"]].rename(columns={"missing": "Missing, n"}),
           "Table 3. Predictor nonresponse in the dentate population.",
           "Missingness is distinguished from documented structural non-consumption. Exploratory extension variables are included in this audit.")
```

Frequency units are converted using seven days/week and 30 days/month. The original Stata weekly-frequency derivation used four weeks per month, equivalent to 28 days after conversion to daily units. Raw quantities and unit codes agree; the month convention explains the two derived predictor differences. An added association sensitivity retains the original conversion. Zero consumption is retained. A no-dairy category distinguishes nonconsumers; fruit and vegetable portions become zero when the corresponding frequency is zero. Statistical imputation occurs only inside prediction training folds. Association models use observed outcomes and complete required covariates. The [variable dictionary](../outputs/tables/variable_dictionary.csv) records source variables, categories and derivation rules.

### Descriptive distributions by caries status

The original manuscript and separate dietary table compared participants without caries, with caries, and overall. The following reconstruction retains those columns and all 27 predictors in the primary dentate cohort. It reports raw counts with survey-weighted column percentages and 95% intervals, or weighted means with 95% intervals and weighted standard deviations. These column percentages describe composition; they are different from caries prevalence within predictor categories. Descriptive intervals do not screen variables for model inclusion.

```{python}
#| label: descriptive-profile
#| echo: false
profile = pd.read_csv(TABLES / "descriptive_profile.csv", keep_default_na=False, na_values=[""])
profile_rows = []
for feature in full_features:
    block = profile.loc[profile.variable.eq(feature)]
    for level in block.level.drop_duplicates():
        levels = block.loc[block.level.eq(level)].set_index("domain")
        result = {"Predictor": feature_labels[feature], "Category / measure": str(level)}
        for domain in ["No caries", "Caries", "Total"]:
            row = levels.loc[domain]
            if row.row_type == "missing":
                text = f'{int(row.missing_n):,} missing / {int(row.domain_n):,}'
            elif row.row_type == "mean":
                text = f'{interval(row, digits=2)}; SD {number(row.weighted_sd, 2)}; n={int(row.observed_n):,}'
            else:
                ci = (f'{number(row.ci_low, 1)}–{number(row.ci_high, 1)}'
                      if pd.notna(row.ci_low) else "CI unavailable at boundary")
                text = f'{int(row.n):,}; {number(row.estimate, 1)}% ({ci})'
            result[domain] = text
        profile_rows.append(result)
show_table(pd.DataFrame(profile_rows), "Descriptive supplement. All 27 predictors by caries status.",
           "Category denominator: observed predictor values within the outcome column. Missing rows use the full outcome-column denominator. Means and percentages use the full examination-phase survey design for variance. No values are imputed for this table. SD describes participant dispersion; it is not a standard error. Original unweighted significance tests are not reused.")
```

## Survey inference and model development

The supplied stratum and primary sampling unit (PSU) identifiers are preserved. `Fexp_F1F2p_Corr` is the **working** examination-stage expansion weight: it matches `Fexp_F2p_Corr` exactly in this release and its availability corresponds to the oral-examination stage. The official phase-selection manual could not be retrieved, so definitive confirmation remains outstanding. The accessible [ENS technical workshop](https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/666227_f822f21ebae44f219a23764b448be668.html) supports using the supplied design variables and constructing the design before subsetting; it is teaching material, not official certification of this weight choice. The [source audit](methodological-sources.md) separates verified observations from documentation gaps.

Descriptive and regression variance estimation starts with the complete examination-phase design before defining analytic domains. Centred PSU score totals provide a first-stage, with-replacement linearization without a finite-population correction. The singleton stratum receives the average variance contribution of non-singleton strata. Metric bootstrap intervals use a different convention: the singleton PSU is fixed because its variance cannot be identified from one observed PSU.

### Common validation and preprocessing

Every algorithm uses the same five outer and three inner PSU-grouped folds, with approximate outcome stratification. Median imputation with numeric missingness indicators, categorical “Missing” values, one-hot encoding, scaling and spline construction are fitted within the applicable training sample. Unknown categories are handled without refitting on held-out participants. Predictive splines use three training-derived quantile knots for age, remaining teeth and water where included. There is no class balancing or full-sample outcome-based feature selection.

Training weights are normalized to mean one. Inner validation minimizes pooled survey-weighted log loss. K-nearest neighbours is an unweighted-training benchmark because its estimator does not accept fitting weights; its tuning and evaluation remain weighted. SVM probabilities use grouped, training-only out-of-fold Platt calibration before refitting the classifier. Numeric preprocessing and calibration never use outer evaluation outcomes.

### Transparent grid amendment

An audit restricted to internal tuning tables found repeated selection of the strongest available regularization. One expanded grid was fixed and the complete nested procedure rerun for every corresponding variant. The audit folds overlap and do not constitute independent experiments. This dataset-informed amendment makes the results exploratory development evidence; it does not justify describing the procedure as wholly prespecified or as external validation.

The reporting focus was corrected on 10 September 2026 to reflect the scientific objective of evaluating all predictor contributions. Water had emerged as a result of interest; its follow-up analyses are retained as exploratory. The comprehensive presentation and joint block permutations were added after the existing model results were available. This change did not retune or add algorithms, and must not be represented as a prospectively specified analysis of a privileged water exposure.

```{python}
#| label: model-grids
#| echo: false
grid_rows = []
for model in main_models:
    spec = model_manifest["models"][model]
    candidate_keys = sorted({key for candidate in spec["candidates"] for key in candidate})
    entries = []
    for key in candidate_keys:
        values = {str(candidate[key]) for candidate in spec["candidates"] if key in candidate}
        try:
            ordered_values = sorted(values, key=float)
        except ValueError:
            ordered_values = sorted(values)
        entries.append(f'{key}: {", ".join(ordered_values)}')
    grid_rows.append({"Algorithm": labels[model], "Candidate values": "; ".join(entries),
                      "Candidates": len(spec["candidates"]), "Weighted fitting": "Yes" if spec["weighted_training"] else "No"})
show_table(pd.DataFrame(grid_rows), "Table 5. Final candidate grids, read from the completed model manifest.",
           "The SVM C range was retained because the internal audit showed no consistent boundary direction. The same expanded grids apply to corresponding feature-block variants. No further expansion was made to pursue a desired result.")
```

### Performance and uncertainty

AUC describes ranking; Brier score and log loss assess probability predictions, with lower values preferred. Calibration-in-the-large is an intercept with slope fixed at one; the reported calibration slope comes from a joint intercept/slope fit. Their ideal values are zero and one, respectively. Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values use a fixed 0.5 threshold, which was not selected as a clinical operating point. Logarithmic scores clip probabilities at the manifest-defined numerical epsilon; AUC and Brier use the original probabilities.

```{python}
#| label: uncertainty-method
#| echo: false
display(Markdown(
    f'The {run["bootstrap_replicates"]:,} shared, stratified rescaled PSU-bootstrap replicates produce paired 95% intervals conditional on the fitted models and fixed fold assignments. '
    'They describe sampling variation in evaluated predictions and exclude variability from redevelopment, retuning and alternative partitions. '
    'Repeated model comparisons and subgroup summaries are exploratory; no multiplicity adjustment is applied.'
))
```

## Contributions and stability of all predictors

All 27 raw predictors are evaluated in held-out folds, retaining the encoded columns of each predictor as a group. Mean increases in weighted Brier score quantify disruption of each fitted classifier; AUC decreases are complementary summaries. Higher positive values indicate greater reliance on that predictor for held-out performance. Negative values mean performance improved after permutation in these evaluations; they do not imply a protective effect. Ranks are compared across folds and model families rather than treated as fixed biological attributes.

Correlation can distribute importance across predictors, and permutation can create unrealistic covariate combinations. These analyses measure model reliance, not a causal effect or the direction of an exposure–outcome association. A predictor can be useful jointly with others while having little individual permutation importance. Conversely, measurable permutation importance does not establish that adding it improves a separately developed model.

```{python}
#| label: importance
#| echo: false
show_figure("correa_predictor_importance")
importance_rows = []
importance_order = all_importance.groupby("feature")["brier_increase"].max().sort_values(ascending=False).index
for feature in importance_order:
    feature_rows = all_importance.loc[all_importance.feature.eq(feature)].set_index("model")
    result = {"Predictor": feature_labels[feature]}
    for model, short in [("random_forest", "RF"), ("spline_logistic", "Spline")]:
        row = feature_rows.loc[model]
        result[f"{short}: ΔBrier"] = number(row.brier_increase, 4)
        result[f"{short}: AUC drop"] = number(row.auc_drop, 4)
        result[f"{short}: median rank (range)"] = f'{row.median_rank:g} ({int(row.best_rank)}–{int(row.worst_rank)})'
        result[f"{short}: top-three folds"] = f'{row.fraction_top3:.0%}'
    importance_rows.append(result)
show_table(pd.DataFrame(importance_rows), "Table 8. Contributions and fold stability of all 27 predictors.",
           "RF = random forest; spline = spline logistic regression. ΔBrier and AUC drop are means using held-out expansion-weight totals. Rank ranges are stability summaries, not confidence intervals. Rows are ordered by the larger mean ΔBrier across the two models; this ordering is descriptive. Complete fold ranges are available in the aggregate importance file.")
shared_leaders = set(importance_leaders["random_forest"].feature) & set(importance_leaders["spline_logistic"].feature)
shared_text = ', '.join(feature_labels[name] for name in sorted(shared_leaders)) if shared_leaders else 'none'
display(Markdown(
    f'The two top-three lists share **{shared_text}**. '
    'Agreement between algorithms supports a model-comparison description; disagreement and broad rank ranges indicate dependence on the fitted functional form and training sample. '
    'The full table retains low, null and negative contributions, avoiding selection of only the most prominent findings.'
))
```

### Joint contributions of predictor blocks

The conceptual blocks are jointly permuted with the same row permutation for all variables in a block. This preserves relationships within that block while disrupting its relationship to the remaining predictors and outcome. Group importance is not the sum of individual importances, and blocks differ in size. It is also distinct from retraining a model after removing a block. The existing random-forest and spline models are reproduced from their selected parameters, with held-out probabilities checked against the saved values; no new algorithm is added.

```{python}
#| label: group-contributions
#| echo: false
group_stability = tables["grouped_importance_stability"]
block_rows = []
block_order = group_stability.groupby("block")["brier_increase"].max().sort_values(ascending=False).index
assert set(block_order) == set(contributions["groups"]), "Group definitions and estimates disagree."
for block in block_order:
    indexed = group_stability.loc[group_stability.block.eq(block)].set_index("model")
    result = {"Block": block, "Predictors": len(contributions["groups"][block])}
    for model, short in [("random_forest", "RF"), ("spline_logistic", "Spline")]:
        row = indexed.loc[model]
        result[f"{short}: ΔBrier (fold range)"] = f'{row.brier_increase:.4f} ({row.minimum_fold_brier_increase:.4f} to {row.maximum_fold_brier_increase:.4f})'
        result[f"{short}: median rank (range)"] = f'{row.median_rank:g} ({int(row.best_rank)}–{int(row.worst_rank)})'
    block_rows.append(result)
show_table(pd.DataFrame(block_rows), "Table 9. Joint permutation importance of conceptual predictor blocks.",
           "Blocks are defined for this exploratory follow-up. Fold ranges are descriptive stability intervals, not confidence intervals. Joint disruption preserves within-block relationships; block sizes differ, so values must not be interpreted as per-variable contributions.")
block_definitions = []
for block, features in contributions["groups"].items():
    block_definitions.append(f'**{block}:** ' + ', '.join(feature_labels[name] for name in features))
display(Markdown('; '.join(block_definitions) + '.'))
show_figure("correa_predictor_groups")
```

## Subgroups and robustness

The six-panel sensitivity figure combines population restrictions and subgroup point estimates with a controlled examination of water encoding. The encoding comparison was added after reviewing the historical scripts and uses the original physical-model hyperparameters, identical outer folds, weights and seeds. Four alternative variants require 20 additional outer fits; the two physical-reference models and their predictions are reused. There is no new hyperparameter search. Nominal categories retain each observed intake as a separate level; they are not low/medium/high groups. The historical index lookup is a fixed, data-derived artifact from the original dentate data, while imputation, scaling, knots and the nominal vocabulary are learned within outer training samples.

## Implications for the manuscript

The manuscript should lead with the contributions of all demographic, dental and dietary predictors to current caries classification. Present both model families, all 27 predictor results and their fold stability, alongside the joint block analyses. Calibration, probability scores and discrimination establish the performance context in which those contributions were measured. A prominent importance rank is a hypothesis-generating finding, not evidence of causation or a reason to make one exposure the study's original objective.

Claims of general algorithm superiority should be tied to the actual comparisons. A small AUC improvement over a linear model does not establish clinically useful discrimination, and a full dietary model need not outperform a simpler demographic/dental model. Correlated predictors and unequal block sizes limit direct attribution. Findings such as water can motivate explicitly secondary analyses; their selection after observing results must remain transparent. No finding here supports a clinical recommendation to increase water intake to prevent caries.

This emphasis is consistent with the distinction between diagnostic and prognostic models, appropriate validation and practical usefulness discussed in the [Caries Research methodological review](https://karger.com/cre/article/doi/10.1159/000553309/952744/Prognostic-Clinical-Predictive-Models-for-Dental). Transparent descriptions of population, missingness, model development and performance also follow the reporting aims of [TRIPOD+AI](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-078378). Neither reference substitutes for evaluation of this dataset or guarantees journal acceptance.

The main limitations are cross-sectional temporality; self-reported predictors, exposure tails and measurement error; selection into the examination and dentate domains; the working, incompletely documented weight choice; singleton-variance conventions; and reliance on a concurrent tooth-count predictor. Importance depends on the fitted model, correlations and the perturbation scheme. The dataset-informed grid amendment, later block analysis and multiple exploratory comparisons add development uncertainty; permutation stability ranges and conditional metric intervals do not cover all of it. There is no temporal or geographic external validation, no assessment of clinical net benefit, and no demonstrated transportability or deployment readiness. The water follow-up additionally lacks measured fluoride exposure, a verified glass volume and temporal ordering.

## Matched comparison using the original paper coding

The reconstructed historical matrix contains 90 columns for 27 predictors in the original 4,994 complete cases. An independent R preprocessing export agrees with the recovered processed-data cache; the production reconstruction and new model fits use Python. The historical representation uses water level indices, fruit/vegetable-day categories with treatment contrasts, original weekly beverage frequencies with four-week months, and the original category reference levels. The current representation retains physical quantities, numerical days and training-fitted one-hot encoding.

Both random-forest variants are newly trained in the same complete cases. They inherit the same five PSU-disjoint outer assignments, weights, seeds and per-fold hyperparameters from the principal forest's outer training data. No new tuning occurs; selection originally used the larger cohort's training portion. This compares the representation package while holding the cohort fixed. It is distinct from the earlier complete-case evaluation of models trained in 5,036 participants and from the water-only sensitivity. It does not recreate the original caret engine or participant-level split.

```{python}

#| echo: false

     "Brier score": f'{r.brier:.6f}', "Log loss": f'{r.log_loss:.6f}'}
    for r in hperf.itertuples()
]), "Historical coding supplement A. Matched random-forest refits.",
"Both models are trained and evaluated in the same 4,994 participants. Intervals are conditional PSU-bootstrap intervals for fixed models and inherited folds.")

show_table(pd.DataFrame([
    {"Metric": r.metric, "Historical minus modern": number(r.difference, 6),
     "Conditional 95% CI": f'{number(r.ci_low, 6)} to {number(r.ci_high, 6)}'}
    for r in hpairs.itertuples()
]), "Historical coding supplement B. Paired performance differences.",
"Positive AUC differences and negative Brier/log-loss differences favour the historical representation. Comparisons are exploratory and do not isolate water from the other coding differences.")

    for r in water_compare.itertuples()

"Each predictor is permuted jointly across its encoded columns using five shared row permutations per held-out fold. Negative values are retained; fold ranges are not confidence intervals.")
show_figure("historical_coding_comparison")
```

The new impurity scores are calculated on the fitted forests, both per column and summed within each original predictor. Those sums remain impurity scores. Held-out permutation instead measures predictive deterioration after perturbing the whole predictor while preserving its category combinations. The recovered 0–100 chart is shown as a separate historical reference, with its legume-category translation corrected; none of the new fits is asserted to reproduce its scores exactly. [Permutation and impurity importance](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/permutation_importance.html).

## Exploratory water associations

Eight survey-weighted association analyses separate effect estimation from algorithm comparison. The primary logistic model estimates a linear water term while adjusting flexibly for age, remaining teeth and soda/juice frequency, plus sex, region, rurality, education, indigenous identification and birthplace. A second model uses a water spline. Further analyses add the three contextual variables, restrict age, assess the exposure tail, omit remaining teeth, estimate a modified Poisson prevalence ratio, or retain the original 28-day beverage conversion. The last analysis was added after source reconciliation. These regressions use complete required covariates, rather than the prediction pipeline's imputation strategy.

```{python}
                       "Measure": water_spline["measure"], "Estimate (95% CI)": interval(water_spline), "p value": number(water_spline.p_value)})
show_table(pd.DataFrame(effect_rows), "Table 13. Adjusted cross-sectional water associations and sensitivity analyses.",
           "All linear estimates compare one additional reported glass/day. The spline row is a conditional odds ratio at identical other covariates. Odds ratios and prevalence ratios are different measures; p values are exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity.")
association_interpretation = (
    "The interval includes no association and remains compatible with modest associations in either direction."
    if water_linear.ci_low <= 1 <= water_linear.ci_high else
    "The interval excludes the null within this model, but cross-sectional adjustment does not establish a causal effect."
)
display(Markdown(
    f'The primary adjusted odds ratio was **{interval(water_linear)} per reported glass/day**. {association_interpretation} '
    f'The spline comparison of {water_spline.comparison_water:g} versus {water_spline.reference_water:g} glasses/day was '
    f'**{interval(water_spline)}**, supported by {int(water_spline.n_at_comparison):,} and {int(water_spline.n_at_reference):,} participants '
    'at those exact intakes, respectively. This contrast is an odds ratio at the same other covariates, not a ratio of standardized prevalences.'
))
legacy_effect = tables["water_effects"].query("model == 'Original 28-day beverage conversion'").iloc[0]
beverage_differences = source["beverage_month_conversion"]["differences"]
display(Markdown(
    f'The original monthly convention changes daily-equivalent soda frequency for '
    f'{beverage_differences["soda_frequency"]["n_different_dentate"]:,} dentate participants and juice frequency for '
    f'{beverage_differences["juice_frequency"]["n_different_dentate"]:,}. '
    f'Retaining those original frequencies gives a water odds ratio of **{interval(legacy_effect)}** '
    f'in {int(legacy_effect["n"]):,} participants. This sensitivity changes the association adjustment only; '
    'the primary nested prediction models retain the declared 30-day convention.'
))
show_figure("water_association")
diagnostics = tables["diagnostics"]
poisson = diagnostics.query("model == 'Modified Poisson prevalence ratio'").iloc[0]
display(Markdown(
    'The adjusted curve averages spline-model predictions over the observed covariate distribution using survey weights. '
    'Its pointwise delta-method intervals propagate design-based coefficient uncertainty **conditional on that fixed covariate composition**; '
    'they do not include uncertainty in the composition itself. '
    f'The modified Poisson model produced **{int(poisson.predictions_above_one):,} fitted values above one**. '
    'Its robust prevalence-ratio coefficient is reported as a sensitivity analysis; those fitted values must not be presented as valid individual probabilities.'
))
```

## Reproducibility and aggregate outputs

The report executes Python against completed aggregate results and stops if required inputs, source hashes, verified reconciliation, cohort checks or the final model grid are inconsistent. Model development and statistical inference are performed by the repository's analysis pipeline; rendering this document does not retrain models. The recovered Stata source remains intact. Participant-level data, held-out predictions and serialized estimators are excluded from this report. All displayed estimates and figures are read from the completed run.

```{python}
#| label: reproducibility
#| echo: false
repro = [
    ("Run status", run["status"]), ("Completed (UTC)", run["completed_utc"]),
    ("Analysis seed", str(run["analysis_seed"])),
    ("Outer / inner folds", f'{run["outer_folds"]} / {run["inner_folds"]}'),
    ("Bootstrap replicates", f'{run["bootstrap_replicates"]:,}'),
    ("Permutation repeats per predictor/fold", str(model_manifest["settings"]["permutation_repeats"])),
    ("Predictor-contribution analysis", contributions["status"]),
    ("Water-encoding sensitivity", encoding["status"]),
    ("Alternative water-encoding outer fits / new tuning searches", f'{encoding["alternative_outer_fits_required"]} / {encoding["new_hyperparameter_searches"]}'),
    ("Joint-permutation seed / repeats", f'{contributions["seed"]} / {contributions["permutation_repeats"]}'),
    ("Largest reproduced-probability difference", f'{max(check["max_absolute_probability_difference"] for check in contributions["refit_checks"]):.2g}'),
    ("Log-probability epsilon", str(model_manifest["settings"]["probability_log_epsilon"])),
    ("Python", run["python"]),
    ("Original Stata source", source["sources"]["original_dta"]["file"]),
    ("Original Stata SHA-256", run["original_input_sha256"]),
    ("Supplementary SPSS SHA-256", run["input_sha256"]),
    ("Source reconciliation", source["status"]),
    ("Original R reference commit", source["sources"]["original_code"]["commit"]),
    ("Supplied stratum / cluster overlap violations", str(int(tables["validation_split_checks"]["psu_overlap"].sum()))),
    ("Statistically imputed outcomes", str(audit["integrity"]["outcomes_imputed"])),
    ("Clipped extreme observations", str(audit["integrity"]["extreme_values_clipped"])),
]
show_table(pd.DataFrame(repro, columns=["Item", "Recorded value"]), "Table 14. Reproducibility record.",
           "Hashes identify both input releases without exposing participant records or private filesystem locations. The original R reference is linked in the provenance section. Fold overlap checks assess shared PSUs across train/test partitions.")
show_table(pd.DataFrame(sorted(run["packages"].items()), columns=["Package", "Version"]),
           "Table 15. Recorded software versions.")
diagnostic_display = diagnostics[["model", "n", "df", "rank", "parameters", "converged", "predictions_above_one"]].copy()
diagnostic_display.columns = ["Association analysis", "n", "Design df", "Rank", "Parameters", "Converged", "Fitted values >1"]
show_table(diagnostic_display, "Table 16. Association-model diagnostics.",
           "Convergence and full rank are necessary numerical checks; they do not validate causal assumptions or exposure measurement. The Poisson diagnostic is discussed in the association section.")
```
